consequence
A result or effect of a particular action or situation, especially one that is unwelcome or bad.
She had to face the consequence of ignoring the school guidelines.
evidence
Facts, information or physical signs that prove whether a statement or belief is true and correct.
The student presented clear evidence to support her main essay argument.
maintain
To make a situation or state of affairs continue in the same way without changing.
It is vital to maintain a regular study schedule before final examinations.
significant
Large or important enough to be noticed, or to have a clear effect on something.
There was a significant improvement in his test marks after extra practice.
contribute
To give something, such as money, ideas or help, in order to achieve a goal.
Every member of the group should contribute fresh ideas to the discussion.
analyse
To examine something in detail in order to understand it or explain its different features.
Students were asked to analyse the causes of the industrial revolution in Britain.
evaluate
To form an opinion about the amount, value or quality of something after careful thought.
Teachers evaluate essay arguments based on structure, clarity and supported facts.
benefit
An advantage or positive effect that something brings to a person or a group.
One major benefit of learning a second language is improved memory skills.
challenge
A new or difficult task that tests someone's ability, skill or mental energy.
Completing the long research project within two weeks was a difficult challenge.
efficient
Working or operating in a quick, organized way without wasting any time or resources.
Using a weekly planner is an efficient way to organize school assignments.
flexible
Able to change or adapt easily to different circumstances, ideas or new plans.
Online courses offer flexible timetables for students who work part-time jobs.
perspective
A particular attitude towards something or a specific way of considering an issue.
The book offers a fresh perspective on historical events in Europe.
obstacle
A situation or object that makes it difficult for someone to achieve something.
Lack of financial funding was a major obstacle to finishing the study.
temporary
Lasting or intended to exist for only a limited period of time, not permanent.
The library closed its main reading room for temporary building repairs.
priority
Something that is regarded as more important than other matters and handled first.
Improving reading comprehension should be the highest priority for young learners.
strategy
A detailed plan of action designed to achieve a long-term goal or success.
The school developed a new strategy to reduce plastic waste on campus.
research
A careful and detailed study of a subject to discover new information or facts.
Scientific research shows that regular exercise improves mental health in adults.
data
Facts or numbers collected together to be examined and used to make decisions.
The researcher gathered relevant statistical data from over five hundred survey respondents.
theory
A formal set of ideas intended to explain why something happens or exists.
Darwin introduced his famous theory of evolution in the nineteenth century.
method
A particular procedure or systematic way of doing something according to a plan.
Interviewing local residents was the main method used in the sociology project.
factor
One of several things that causes or influences a situation or final outcome.
Dietary habits are an important factor affecting overall physical health and energy.
process
A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular result.
Learning a musical instrument is a slow process that requires daily effort.
require
To need something for a specific purpose or because of a rule or law.
Most academic essay assignments require students to cite their background sources accurately.
achieve
To succeed in reaching a target or completing something through effort and skill.
Students can achieve high examination scores if they review their notes daily.
affect
To produce a change or influence the way something develops or behaves.
Lack of adequate sleep can negatively affect student performance during morning exams.
effect
A change or result that occurs because of a specific cause or event.
The positive effect of regular exercise on mood is well documented.
increase
To become larger in amount, number, size or degree over a period.
The population of urban areas continues to increase every single year.
reduce
To make something smaller or less in size, amount, degree or importance.
Cycling to work helps to reduce carbon emissions in busy city centres.
compare
To examine two or more things to identify similarities and differences between them.
The essay asks us to compare traditional learning with modern online education.
contrast
To place two things together in order to show their differences clearly.
In her speech, she chose to contrast rural life with urban living.
similar
Having characteristics that are almost the same, but not completely identical in nature.
Both brothers have very similar views on environmental protection and recycling.
different
Not the same as another thing or person; separate and distinct in character.
The two scientists reached completely different conclusions despite using the same data.
advantage
A condition or feature that gives someone or something a higher chance of success.
Speaking several languages gives job applicants a clear advantage in global business.
disadvantage
A condition or situation that causes difficulty or reduces the chances of success.
One disadvantage of living far from school is the long daily commute.
solution
A way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation successfully.
Engineers are working hard to find a sustainable solution to water pollution.
cause
A person, event or thing that makes something happen, especially something negative.
Heavy snowfall was the primary cause of traffic delays across the region.
result
An outcome or consequence that occurs because of something else that happened before.
Her excellent final score was the direct result of months of studying.
in addition
Used to introduce an extra piece of information or another supporting argument.
In addition to reading textbooks, students should practice writing practice essays.
on the other hand
Used to introduce a point or idea that contrasts with one previously mentioned.
Public transport is affordable; on the other hand, driving a car is faster.
as a result
Used to explain that something happened because of an event mentioned before.
The heavy rain flooded the streets, and as a result, schools were closed.
in conclusion
Used at the end of an essay or speech to state final summary points.
In conclusion, renewable energy is essential for protecting the future of our planet.
for instance
Used when giving a specific example to support a statement or claim.
Many European cities, for instance Vienna, have excellent public transportation networks.
in contrast
Used to show that two ideas, facts or situations are very different.
In contrast to her brother, who loves maths, she prefers studying literature.
furthermore
In addition to what has already been stated; also used to add emphasis.
The library has expanded its hours; furthermore, computer access is now free.
for example
Used when introducing a concrete case or illustration of a general idea.
Several fruits, for example apples and oranges, contain high amounts of vitamin C.
in summary
Used to introduce a brief statement containing the main points of a text.
In summary, the experiment proved that plants grow faster under direct sunlight.
moreover
Used to add an important extra fact or reason to support an argument.
The car is fuel-efficient; moreover, its maintenance costs are exceptionally low.
as a consequence
As an outcome or effect of something that has just been described.
He forgot his passport and, as a consequence, missed his flight abroad.
despite this
Used to show that something happened although something else might have prevented it.
The weather was cold and rainy; despite this, they enjoyed their outdoor hike.
on the contrary
Used to state that the opposite of what was just said is true.
The task was not boring; on the contrary, it was highly engaging.
in general
Usually or in most situations, considering the overall situation rather than details.
In general, students who attend every lecture achieve better final examination marks.
in comparison
When compared with another thing or situation to highlight differences or similarities.
In comparison to last year, overall company profits have increased by ten percent.
in fact
Used to give more detailed information or to correct a mistaken impression.
The test was not easy; in fact, many candidates struggled with section two.
nevertheless
Despite what has just been said or referred to in a discussion; even so.
The weather was extremely cold; nevertheless, they decided to continue their walk.
above all
Most importantly, or before considering any other factors in a given situation.
Above all, young drivers should remain focused and avoid taking unnecessary risks.
owing to
Because of a particular reason or situation that has already been mentioned.
Owing to heavy rain, the outdoor sports event was postponed until next week.
due to
Because of a specific reason, event or circumstance that caused an outcome.
The flight was delayed due to technical difficulties with the aircraft engine.
according to
As stated by a specific person, official report, document or authority.
According to the latest weather forecast, it will rain throughout the weekend.
with regard to
Concerning or in connection with a specific subject or topic under discussion.
With regard to your application, we are pleased to offer you an interview.
in terms of
In relation to a particular aspect, measurement or point of view.
In terms of popularity, football remains the most watched sport in Britain.
as well as
In addition to someone or something else; together with another factor.
The course covers academic writing as well as listening and speaking skills.
so as to
In order to achieve a specific intention, purpose or desired final result.
She left home early so as to avoid the heavy morning traffic jams.
in order to
For the purpose of doing or achieving a specific action or objective.
Students must register online in order to access the university library facilities.
in view of
Taking a particular fact or circumstance into consideration before making a decision.
In view of recent budget cuts, the department had to cancel the trip.
all things considered
Taking every aspect and detail into account before forming a final judgment.
All things considered, the event was a great success for our team.
assess
To judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount or value of something.
Teachers use final written examinations to assess student progress throughout the year.
examine
To inspect or study something carefully in order to discover facts or information.
Doctors need to examine the patient thoroughly before recommending a suitable treatment.
demonstrate
To show clearly that something exists or is true by providing proof.
The recent research findings demonstrate that regular sleep improves memory retention significantly.
indicate
To show, point out or make something clear using evidence or signs.
Dark clouds in the sky indicate that a heavy rainstorm is approaching.
illustrate
To explain or make something clear by using examples, diagrams or pictures.
The speaker used historical facts to illustrate his point during the lecture.
suggest
To mention an idea, plan or possibility for people to consider carefully.
Recent study findings suggest that eating breakfast daily aids cognitive concentration.
establish
To set up, create or discover something on a firm and permanent basis.
Scientists hope to establish clear guidelines for reducing carbon emissions in industry.
identify
To recognize and name a particular person, object, problem or essential feature.
The purpose of the study was to identify key factors influencing student motivation.
define
To state or describe clearly the exact meaning of a word or concept.
Dictionaries define vocabulary terms to help language learners understand proper word usage.
determine
To discover the facts about something or calculate an exact answer or cause.
Investigators tried to determine the exact cause of the unexpected power failure.
propose
To suggest a plan, idea or scheme for other people to consider.
The committee decided to propose new rules to improve public transport safety.
clarify
To make something clearer and easier to understand by providing extra explanation.
The professor offered to clarify the instructions for the written term essay.
confirm
To state or show that a belief, opinion or fact is definitely true.
Laboratory tests were able to confirm the presence of clean groundwater nearby.
consider
To think carefully about something before making a choice, decision or judgment.
You should consider all potential options before deciding on a university degree.
discuss
To talk or write about a subject in detail, giving different views.
Students gathered after class to discuss the main themes of the novel.
emphasise
To give special importance, value or attention to a particular point or fact.
Teachers always emphasise the importance of checking essay work for spelling mistakes.
highlight
To draw special attention to an important piece of information or idea.
The report served to highlight key challenges facing the local healthcare system.
imply
To suggest that something is true without stating it directly or explicitly.
Her silence seemed to imply that she agreed with the proposed solution.
justify
To give a good reason or explanation for an action, decision or belief.
It is difficult to justify spending so much money on unnecessary luxuries.
outline
To give a brief description of the main facts or ideas of something.
The supervisor asked him to outline his essay plan before writing it.
state
To express information, facts or an opinion clearly and formally in speech or writing.
Applicants must state their full name and address on the official form.
summarise
To express the main points of something in a short and concise form.
At the end of the presentation, she will summarise the main conclusions.
address
To deal with or give attention to a problem, issue or question.
The government must address the rising cost of living in major cities.
adopt
To accept or start using a new method, idea, plan or attitude.
Schools should adopt modern digital tools to enhance student learning experiences.
modify
To make small changes to something in order to improve or correct it.
The architect had to modify the original building plans to meet safety standards.
transform
To completely change the appearance, character or quality of something for the better.
The new green park will transform the neglected town centre completely.
enhance
To increase or improve the quality, value, attractiveness or strength of something.
Adding descriptive adjectives can enhance the overall quality of your written work.
promote
To encourage the growth, development or popular adoption of a particular cause.
The campaign aims to promote healthy eating habits among primary school children.
encourage
To give someone support, confidence or hope to do or achieve something.
Good teachers always encourage their students to ask questions during classroom discussions.
support
To agree with, help or approve of an idea, person or statement.
The survey data helped to support the claim made by the researchers.
argue
To give reasons to support or oppose an opinion, belief or idea.
Some experts argue that technology reduces the amount of face-to-face communication.
claim
To state that something is true, often without providing immediate proof.
He continues to claim that he completed the entire assignment without help.
assume
To accept that something is true without having proof or full evidence.
Many people assume that learning a language becomes impossible after childhood.
predict
To say that a particular event or outcome will happen in the future.
Weather experts predict heavy rainfall across the southern coast tomorrow morning.
conclude
To decide or reach an opinion after considering all relevant facts and evidence.
After reviewing the evidence, the judge will conclude the trial today.
observe
To watch someone or something carefully in order to learn or notice facts.
Scientists set up cameras to observe wild animals in their natural habitat.
describe
To say or write what someone or something is like in detail.
The witness was asked to describe the vehicle involved in the accident.
investigate
To examine a crime, problem or statement carefully to discover the truth.
Police officers will investigate the sudden disappearance of the valuable artwork.
explore
To travel through or examine a topic carefully to learn more about it.
The essay will explore the economic effects of renewable energy adoption.
perceive
To notice, see or understand something in a particular way through the senses.
Different cultures may perceive time and punctuality in surprisingly varied ways.
recognise
To accept or acknowledge the existence, truth or value of something formally.
It is important to recognise the hard work of all volunteers involved.
represent
To act or speak officially on behalf of a person, group or country.
Diplomats represent their nation during international peace negotiations and meetings.
reflect
To show, express or be a clear sign of a particular situation or feeling.
Her essay answers reflect a deep understanding of complex historical events.
interpret
To explain or understand the meaning of information, actions or text clearly.
Scholars often interpret ancient texts in different ways based on new findings.
refine
To improve something by making small adjustments or removing minor defects.
She took time to refine her draft before submitting the final version.
adapt
To change your behaviour or ideas so as to fit new conditions successfully.
Species must adapt to changing environments in order to survive over time.
integrate
To combine two or more things so that they work together effectively.
The new curriculum aims to integrate digital technology with traditional classroom activities.
implement
To start using a plan, system or law officially so that it happens.
The city council plans to implement new traffic regulations next month.
generate
To produce or create something, such as electricity, ideas or income.
Solar panels generate clean electricity by absorbing sunlight throughout the day.
provide
To give something to someone or make it available for their use.
Libraries provide free access to thousands of books and online learning resources.
dispute
To question whether a statement, fact or claim is true or valid.
Historians continue to dispute the exact date when the ancient monument was built.
criticise
To express disapproval or point out faults and mistakes in something.
Reviewers began to criticise the film for its predictable plot and weak dialogue.
reject
To refuse to accept, use, believe or agree to a proposal or idea.
The university committee had to reject the proposal due to insufficient funding.
defend
To protect or provide arguments to support an opinion, decision or statement.
Students must defend their thesis statement during the final oral examination.
resolve
To find an acceptable solution to a problem, argument or difficult situation.
Mediators worked tirelessly to resolve the disagreement between the two companies.
review
To examine or study something again carefully to check or improve it.
Students should review their study notes thoroughly every evening before sleeping.
apply
To make practical use of a rule, method, idea or piece of knowledge.
You can apply these grammar rules when writing your formal essay assignments.
attempt
To try to do something, especially something difficult or challenging.
He decided to attempt the advanced mathematics exam despite its high difficulty.
classify
To arrange or divide things into groups according to their shared features.
Biologists classify living organisms into distinct categories based on shared traits.
calculate
To use mathematical operations to discover an amount, price or number.
Students must calculate the exact average score from the given data set.
construct
To build, make or put together something complex using various parts.
Engineers plan to construct a new bridge across the river next year.
convince
To succeed in making someone believe that something is true or right.
She managed to convince her parents that studying abroad was a great opportunity.
display
To show or arrange something clearly so that people can see it easily.
Museums display rare historical artefacts for visitors to admire and study.
distribute
To give or share something out among a specific group of people or organisations.
Volunteers arrived to distribute food supplies and warm clothes to local families.
estimate
To form an approximate judgment or calculation about an amount or value.
Experts estimate that the repair work will cost over ten thousand pounds.
expand
To become greater in size, amount, number, scope or importance.
The school plans to expand its science laboratory to accommodate more students.
expose
To make something visible or known by removing a cover or hiding place.
Investigative journalists work to expose corruption in public institutions and governments.
extend
To make something longer, larger or last for a greater period of time.
The headteacher agreed to extend the deadline for submitting the science project.
influence
To affect or change how someone thinks, behaves or develops in life.
Parents strongly influence their children's attitudes towards reading and education.
inform
To give someone facts or official information concerning a particular subject or event.
The school will inform parents about the upcoming field trip by email.
inspect
To look closely at something to check its condition or quality carefully.
Safety officers arrived to inspect the building equipment before work resumed.
perform
To carry out an action, task or piece of work successfully.
Surgeons must perform delicate operations with extreme care and precision.
overcome
To succeed in dealing with or controlling a problem or difficulty.
She managed to overcome her fear of public speaking through regular practice.
persuade
To cause someone to do or believe something by giving good reasons.
The advertisement tried to persuade consumers to buy energy-efficient appliances.
preserve
To keep something safe in its original state or good condition.
Efforts are being made to preserve historic buildings in the city centre.
replace
To take the place of something or put a new thing in its position.
Electric buses will eventually replace old diesel vehicles across the entire city.
reveal
To make something known that was previously secret, hidden or unknown.
The survey results reveal a significant increase in public interest in science.
specify
To state or name something clearly, explicitly and in exact detail.
Contract documents must specify the exact materials to be used for construction.
sustain
To cause or allow something to continue for a period without failing.
Regular rainfall is necessary to sustain agriculture in dry rural regions.
undergo
To experience or suffer a process, change, test or medical treatment.
The hospital patient had to undergo several medical tests before leaving.
impact
A powerful effect or influence that something has on a situation or person.
The opening of the new library had a positive impact on literacy rates.
issue
An important topic or problem that people are discussing or arguing about.
Climate change is a critical global issue that requires immediate international action.
aspect
A particular part, feature or quality of a situation, problem or subject.
One positive aspect of urban living is easy access to cultural venues.
concept
An abstract or general idea of something that exists or is formed.
The concept of sustainable development balances economic growth with nature conservation.
context
The situation, background or environment in which something happens or exists.
To understand the poem fully, you must consider its historical context.
trend
A general direction in which a situation is changing or developing over time.
There is a growing trend towards working remotely from home across Europe.
approach
A particular way of considering, dealing with or starting to solve something.
The school adopted a holistic approach to student health and overall well-being.
category
A group of things or people that share similar characteristics or qualities.
Each library book is placed in a specific category according to topic.
feature
A noticeable or important characteristic, quality or part of something.
The most prominent feature of the new stadium is its retractable glass roof.
function
The special purpose or job that something is designed to perform.
The main function of the heart is to pump blood throughout the body.
structure
The way in which parts are organized or arranged to form a whole.
The essay lacked a clear structure, making it difficult to follow the argument.
source
A place, person or document from which specific information or material originates.
The river is the main source of fresh water for the surrounding town.
access
The opportunity or right to use, enter or obtain something easily.
All university students have free access to digital journals and online books.
alternative
A choice or option that is different from the usual or main one.
Solar energy provides a clean alternative to traditional fossil fuels.
authority
The power or official right to give orders, make decisions and enforce rules.
The local council has the authority to approve new housing developments.
capacity
The maximum amount or number that something can contain, produce or handle.
The theater reached its full capacity of five hundred people during the show.
attitude
A settled way of thinking or feeling about someone or something in life.
Having a positive attitude towards study can greatly improve your exam performance.
circumstances
The facts, events or conditions that affect and surround a situation.
Under normal circumstances, final exam results are published within three weeks.
community
A group of people living in the same place or sharing common interests.
The local community worked together to restore the old neighborhood park.
condition
The physical state of something or the general state of current affairs.
The vintage car was restored and is now in excellent working condition.
conflict
A serious disagreement, argument or struggle between people, groups or nations.
The two countries tried to resolve their border conflict through peaceful diplomacy.
contribution
Something that you give or do to help produce or achieve something.
Her research made a valuable contribution to our understanding of plant growth.
debate
A formal discussion or argument on a particular topic in a public meeting.
Members of parliament engaged in a heated debate over educational funding.
decision
A choice or judgment that you make after thinking about several possibilities.
Choosing which university to attend is an important decision for young adults.
decline
A continuous decrease in the quality, quantity, value or strength of something.
The region experienced a sharp decline in manufacturing jobs over the decade.
definition
A statement expressing the exact meaning of a word, phrase or concept.
The dictionary provides a concise definition for every common academic term.
demand
The total amount of a good or service that people want to buy.
High consumer demand led to a shortage of electric bicycles in stores.
development
The process of growing, changing, becoming larger or more advanced over time.
Proper nutrition is essential for the healthy physical development of growing children.
distinction
A clear difference or contrast between two similar things or concepts.
It is important to make a distinction between opinion and proven fact.
diversity
The condition of including many different types of people, ideas or things.
Cultural diversity enriches society by introducing varied traditions, perspectives and customs.
element
A fundamental or essential part of a whole system, plan or situation.
Clear communication is a vital element of successful teamwork on projects.
emphasis
Special attention, weight or importance given to a particular point or detail.
The school puts great emphasis on developing foreign language skills early.
environment
The natural conditions such as air, water and land in which creatures live.
Pollution poses a severe threat to the fragile marine environment everywhere.
error
A mistake or fault in calculation, judgment, writing or computer processing.
The accounting team discovered a minor calculation error in the monthly report.
expansion
The act or process of becoming larger in size, area or scope.
The rapid expansion of the city resulted in increased demand for housing.
experience
Knowledge or skill gained by doing, seeing or feeling things over time.
Working abroad gave her valuable international experience in marketing and business.
facility
A building, room or piece of equipment provided for a particular purpose.
The new sports facility includes a swimming pool, gym and running track.
focus
The main centre of interest, activity, attention or effort in something.
The main focus of the meeting was improving workplace safety standards.
goal
An objective or target that a person or organisation hopes to achieve.
Her primary goal for the year is to pass all her examinations.
growth
The process of increasing in physical size, value, number or economic power.
Economic growth slowed down following the unexpected rise in global energy prices.
guideline
A piece of advice or rule giving guidance on how to act properly.
The ministry issued a new guideline for safe internet use in schools.
idea
A thought, plan, opinion or mental picture formed inside the human mind.
She came up with a brilliant idea for reducing food waste at school.
image
A picture, representation or mental visual impression of a person or object.
The satellite captured a detailed image of the storm approaching the coastline.
importance
The quality of being worthy of note, attention, value or significant concern.
Teachers frequently stress the importance of daily reading for vocabulary building.
improvement
The process of making something better or the state of being improved.
The student showed noticeable improvement in her writing skills this term.
incentive
Something that encourages or motivates a person to work harder or act.
The company offered a financial incentive to employees who met sales targets.
income
Money received, especially on a regular basis, for work or through investments.
The family relies on a steady monthly income to pay their living expenses.
information
Facts or details learned or provided about something or someone.
The website provides useful information about admission requirements for international applicants.
innovation
The introduction of new ideas, methods, devices or creative solutions.
Technological innovation has revolutionized how people communicate across the globe daily.
insight
A deep, clear or sudden understanding of a complex situation or problem.
The lecture provided valuable insight into how human brains process language.
institution
An established organization or foundation devoted to education, public service or law.
The university is a prestigious educational institution with a long historical background.
intention
A goal, purpose or plan that guides a person's intended future actions.
It was never her intention to cause any misunderstanding among group members.
interaction
Communication or direct involvement between two or more people, groups or things.
Social interaction plays a crucial role in early childhood emotional development.
interest
The feeling of wanting to give your attention to something or learn more.
She expressed a keen interest in studying environmental science at university level.
knowledge
Information, understanding and skills acquired through education, study or experience.
Practical experience combined with theoretical knowledge leads to professional success in careers.
limitation
A rule, factor or condition that restricts or controls what can be done.
Budgetary limitation prevented the team from buying state-of-the-art laboratory equipment.
location
A particular place or position where something is situated or happens.
The hotel is in an ideal location near the historical city centre.
majority
The larger number or part of a group, consisting of more than half.
The majority of students voted in favour of extending library opening hours.
measure
An official action taken in order to achieve a particular result or goal.
The government introduced a new measure to reduce plastic bag usage in shops.
minority
The smaller part of a group, consisting of less than half the total.
Only a small minority of citizens preferred the old public transport system.
motive
A reason for doing something, especially one that is kept hidden.
The detective questioned the suspect to discover his true motive for the crime.
option
A choice or possibility that is available to be selected or chosen.
Students have the option to study either French or German in year eight.
outcome
The final result, effect or consequence of an action, event or process.
The final outcome of the negotiation depended on both sides reaching an agreement.
participant
A person who takes part in an activity, event, study or competition.
Each participant in the marathon received a commemorative medal upon finishing the race.
pattern
A repeated or regular way in which something happens, develops or is done.
Scientists noticed a regular pattern in the migration habits of coastal birds.
percentage
An amount or rate expressed as a fraction of one hundred.
A high percentage of respondents expressed satisfaction with the new bus service.
period
A length or portion of time characterized by particular events or conditions.
The country experienced a long period of rapid economic growth in the nineties.
phenomenon
A fact or event that can be observed and studied, especially an unusual one.
Global warming is a complex climate phenomenon affecting weather systems world wide.
policy
A set of ideas or plans agreed upon officially by an organisation.
The school updated its attendance policy to reduce unexcused student absences.
population
All the people or animals living in a particular area, city or country.
The total population of the town has grown steadily over the last decade.
position
The place where someone or something is located, or a social status.
She was promoted to a senior managerial position after three years of work.
possibility
A chance or likelihood that something may happen or be true.
There is a strong possibility of snow during the upcoming winter holiday.
potential
Qualities or abilities that may be developed and lead to future success.
The young athlete displays great potential for becoming an international champion.
practice
The actual application or execution of an idea, method or professional skill.
Putting theoretical ideas into practice requires careful planning and continuous effort.
principle
A fundamental truth, rule or law that serves as the foundation for beliefs.
Honesty is a basic principle that should guide all interpersonal relationships.
probability
The likelihood or chance that a particular event or outcome will happen.
There is a high probability of rain tomorrow according to weather forecasts.
problem
A matter or situation regarded as unwelcome or harmful and needing a solution.
Traffic congestion remains a major urban problem in almost every capital city.
progress
Movement forward or development towards a better, more complete state.
The student made steady progress in learning English grammar over the academic term.
proportion
A part, share or number considered in comparative relation to a whole.
A high proportion of the school budget is spent on upgrading IT facilities.
proposal
A formal suggestion or plan put forward for consideration or discussion by others.
The committee reviewed the written proposal for building a new community library.
purpose
The reason for which something is done, created or exists in life.
The main purpose of the research project was to measure water purity.
range
A variety or set of different things of the same general type.
The shop offers a wide range of organic foods and household products.
reaction
An action or feeling produced in response to something that happened.
His unexpected news produced a surprised reaction from everyone present at dinner.
reason
A cause, explanation or justification for an event, action or belief.
The main reason for his absence was a sudden severe illness.
reform
The improvement or change of a system, law or organisation for better.
The government announced a major educational reform to modernize school curricula.
relationship
The way in which two or more people, groups or things are connected.
Research shows a close relationship between regular physical activity and good mental health.

brief
Of short duration, concise, using only a few words to express something clearly.
The speaker gave a brief summary of the main points before answering questions.
broad
Having a wide range, extent or distance from one side to another.
The course covers a broad spectrum of topics in modern European history.
central
Of greatest importance, principal, or situated directly in the middle area of something.
The central theme of the novel revolves around friendship and loyalty.
certain
Known to be true without doubt, confident, or specific but unnamed.
It is certain that regular practice leads to noticeable skill improvement.
clear
Easy to perceive, understand or interpret clearly, transparent and without any doubt.
Her essay presented a clear argument supported by reliable academic evidence.
common
Occurring, found or done very often, shared by two or more people.
Colds are a common illness during the cold winter months in Europe.
considerable
Notably large in size, amount, extent, degree or importance.
The renovation project required a considerable amount of time and money.
constant
Occurring continuously over a period of time, unchanging or faithful.
The constant noise from the nearby highway made sleeping quite difficult.
continuous
Forming an unbroken whole without interruption or stop over time.
The machine requires a continuous supply of electricity to operate properly.
conventional
Based on or in accordance with what is generally done or believed.
He chose a conventional career path in law after graduating from university.
critical
Expressing adverse or disapproving comments, or crucial to success.
Critical thinking skills enable students to evaluate arguments logically and objectively.
cultural
Relating to the ideas, customs and social behaviour of a society.
Visiting museums is a great way to experience local cultural heritage.
distinct
Recognizably different in nature from something else of similar type.
The two bird species have distinct feather markings that make identification easy.
dramatic
Sudden, striking, impressive, theatrical or emotional in effect or appearance.
There was a dramatic fall in temperatures following the cold weather front.
economic
Relating to economics, economy, trade, industry or financial matters.
The country introduced new economic policies to stimulate trade and business growth.
effective
Successful in producing a desired or intended result or effect.
Using flashcards is an effective method for memorizing new foreign vocabulary.
equal
Being the same in quantity, size, degree, value or status.
All citizens should enjoy equal rights and opportunities under the national law.
equivalent
Equal in value, amount, function, meaning or significance to another.
One mile is roughly equivalent to one point six kilometers in distance.
evident
Plain or obvious to the eye or mind, clearly seen and easily understood.
Her talent for painting was evident from a very early age.
exact
Not different from or less than, strictly accurate or correct in every detail.
Please measure the exact length of the wooden board before cutting it.
existing
In present existence, current, present or available at this time.
The new regulations will apply to all existing building structures in city.
extreme
Reaching a high or highest degree, severe, far beyond normal.
Mountaineers must prepare carefully for extreme weather conditions on high peaks.
familiar
Well known from long or close association, very easy to recognize instantly.
The song sounded familiar, but she could not recall its title.
formal
Done in strict accordance with rules of convention, social etiquette or official requirements.
Write a formal letter of application when applying for academic university courses.
general
Affecting or concerning all or most people, places or things, broad.
In general terms, the economy is performing better than previously expected.
global
Relating to the whole world, worldwide, comprehensive or total.
Climate change is a global issue requiring international cooperation among all nations.
historic
Famous or important in history, belonging to a significant period in the past.
The signing of the peace treaty was a historic moment for humanity.
ideal
Satisfying one's conception of what is completely perfect, most suitable or desirable.
The quiet seaside town is an ideal location for a restful holiday.
identical
Similar in every detail, exactly alike, duplicated in appearance.
The twins wore identical outfits to the family birthday party celebration.
important
Of great significance or value, likely to have profound effect.
Eating a balanced diet is important for maintaining long-term physical health.
independent
Free from outside control, not depending on another's authority or support.
She became financially independent after securing her first full-time job position.
individual
Single, separate, relating to a particular person or thing distinctly.
Each individual student received personal feedback on their term research paper.
inevitable
Certain to happen, completely unavoidable, incapable of being prevented or stopped by anyone.
Change is an inevitable part of life that everyone must learn to accept.
logical
According to the strict rules of logic or formal reasoning, sensible and clear.
His argument followed a logical structure that was easy for listeners to follow.
maximum
As great, high or intense as possible or permitted, representing the upper limit.
The maximum speed limit on British motorways is seventy miles per hour.
